# English (Grade 11, Papers 1 and 2) — Two-Pass Report

**Run:** `20260914T081202Z_864a` · **Status:** completed_with_review · **Generated by:** `scripts/run_english_pass2.py`

## What was processed

* Pass 1 rebuilt at question level from **five verified paper+memo pairs** (126 question records);
  the inherited document-level stubs were replaced, not extended.
* Pairing was verified from printed evidence only: identical DATE/MARKS/EXAMINER blocks where printed,
  printed section headings, the printed cover row, and per-item bracketed marks checked in both documents.
  The July 2014 Paper 2 memorandum prints no header at all, so it was paired on identical numbered content
  and marks plus its Phase-2 inventory record; that fact is recorded in the record itself.
* Every question record stores the SHA-256 of its paper and memorandum and the ORC source IDs resolved from
  `data/raw/english/SOURCE_INVENTORY.yaml`; the builder fails closed if any of these is missing or ambiguous.
* Source defects (printed totals that disagree with their own items, mis-numbered items, an absent Question 5
  marking section) are declared in the batch and never padded, renamed or silently corrected.

## Trust boundary

Everything below is derived from the papers and memoranda in `data/organized/english`. No outside knowledge,
no syllabus and no curriculum coverage is asserted. Every Tier 2/Tier 3 claim carries the source IDs it rests on
and every model remains `unvalidated`, `version 0.1.0-draft`.

Paper 1 (Language) and Paper 2 (Literature/Writing) competences are kept in separate families; no family
mixes the two papers. The confidence rule is the written one — high requires four or more members across
three or more papers — and it classifies 8 of 15 families as high and
7 as medium. That is more 'high' than the corpus expectation of mostly medium families: three Paper 1
sittings in this batch share the same section structure, so several operations genuinely recur across three
papers. The label is arithmetic, not a claim about validity, and every model stays unvalidated.

## What was deliberately not used

* 26 records depend on images (advertisements, cartoons, maps, logos). Their text and memorandum answers are kept in Pass 1, but none may carry a family claim.
* 13 records (three summaries, two essays, four transactional options, and the four November 2016 visual-literacy items) have no marking evidence at all; no marking requirement was invented for them.
* Two records are marked against an IEB rubric that the supplied memoranda do not print; no rubric descriptors were fabricated.
* 45 records remain unassigned (a view over the batch, not a partition): the image-dependent, no-evidence and rubric-only sets above, plus five single-exemplar operations listed in the unresolved items.
* The set texts are text-specific (The God of Small Things in one sitting, Othello in another), so no "theme in [text]" family was admitted.

files print a header date is wrong for this corpus (19 of 21 print one), and that four unpaired papers print
cover rows that disagree with their own header marks.

## Method limits

* Pass 1 transcription is manual reading of the extracted text layer; the mechanical builder only verifies
  the printed anchors (headers, headings, cover rows, per-item marks), the source hashes and the ORC resolution.
* Image-dependent pages were not visually inspected; their records are flagged rather than interpreted.
* Pass 2 models are paper-and-memorandum derivations. They have not been checked against learner scripts or a teacher.
